3:17 (single) | label = Dunhill | writer = Hoyt Axton, Chuck Negron | producer = Richard Podolor | prev_title = One Man Band | prev_year = 1970 | next_title = Liar | next_year = 1971 | misc = {{External music video|header=Official audio|{{YouTube|EVcpKjXYa5c|"Joy to the World" by Three Dog Night}}}} }} "Joy to the World" is a song written by Hoyt Axton and made famous by the rock band Three Dog Night. The song is also popularly known by its opening lyric, "Jeremiah was a bullfrog". Three Dog Night originally released the song on their fourth studio album, Naturally, in November 1970, and subsequently released an edited version of the song as a single in February 1971. The song, which has been described by members of Three Dog Night as a "kid's song" and a "silly song", topped the singles charts in North America, was certified gold by the RIAA, and has since been covered by multiple artists.

sections.heading: Background and recording
sections.wikitext:
[[File:Three Dog Night 1972.JPG|thumb|upright|Three Dog Night, 1972]]
Some of the words are nonsensical. Axton wanted to persuade his record producers to record a new melody he had written, and the producers asked him to sing any words to the tune. A member of Three Dog Night said that the original lyrics to the song were "[[Jeremiah]] was a prophet" but no one liked it.<ref>{{cite news |date=August 20, 2008 |title=Three Dog Night Headlines the Fair Tonight |newspaper=[[The Review (Bainbridge Island)|Bainbridge Island Review]] |at=Entertainment section |issn=1053-2889 |access-date=April 5, 2011 |url=http://www.pnwlocalnews.com/kitsap/bir/entertainment/27111724.html?period=W&mpStartDate=05-15-2010|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120909092628/http://www.pnwlocalnews.com/kitsap/bir/entertainment/27111724.html?period=W&mpStartDate=05-15-2010|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 9, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stereogum.com/2029846/the-number-ones-three-dog-nights-joy-to-the-world/columns/the-number-ones/|title=The Number Ones: Three Dog Night's "Joy To The World"|website=Stereogum.com|date=28 January 2019|access-date=26 December 2021}}</ref>

When Hoyt Axton performed the song to the group, two of the three main vocalists – [[Danny Hutton]] and [[Cory Wells]] – rejected the song, but [[Chuck Negron]] felt that the band needed a "silly song" to help bring the band back together as a working unit. Negron also felt that the song "wasn't even close to our best record, but it might have been one of our most honest."<ref name="notes2" />

The song was recorded by Three Dog Night at American Recording Company, produced by [[Richard Podolor]], and engineered by Bill Cooper.<ref name="notes1" /> Unlike most Three Dog Night songs recorded at that point, instead of having just the three main vocalists singing harmony, the song was recorded with all seven members of the band singing.<ref name="notes2" /> Drummer [[Floyd Sneed]] sings the low-pitched lyric "I wanna tell you" towards the end of the song.

When the song hit number one on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] in 1971, Axton and his mother, [[Mae Axton]], became the first mother and son to each have written a number one pop single in the rock era. Mae Axton co-wrote "[[Heartbreak Hotel]]", which was the first number one hit for [[Elvis Presley]].

sections.heading: Lawsuit
sections.wikitext: In a 1994 case, David P. Jackson filed suit<ref>{{cite web|url=http://law.justia.com/cases/federal/appellate-courts/F3/25/884/572096/|title=Jackson v. Axton|website=Law.justia.com|access-date=2016-10-04}}</ref> claiming co-authorship of the song and alleging that Axton fraudulently claimed sole authorship. In the suit, Jackson claimed that Axton regularly credited him with co-authorship. The [[United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit]] ruled in favor of Axton.  Axton's lawyers included entertainment litigator [[Jeffrey D. Goldman]].

The single had been out less than two months, when on April 9, 1971, "Joy to the World" was certified gold by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]], for shipments of over one million units across the United States.<ref>{{cite certification|region=United States|type=single|artist=Three Dog Night|title=Joy to the World|access-date=April 8, 2013}}</ref> The record was also given a Gold Leaf award by ''[[RPM (magazine)|RPM]]'' magazine for sales of over a million units.<ref>{{cite magazine |date=August 21, 1971 |title=Highlights of ABC/Dunhill Convention |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |volume= 83 |issue= 34 |page=50 |access-date=April 6, 2011 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vwgEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA50 }}</ref> The record won the award for the Best Selling Hit Single Record by the [[National Association of Recording Merchandisers]] in March 1972.<ref>{{cite magazine |date=March 18, 1972 |title=NARM Award Winners |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |volume= 84 |issue= 12 |page=12 |editor1-first=John |editor1-last=Sippel |access-date=April 6, 2011 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jCgEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA12 }}</ref>
It was also ranked by ''Billboard'' magazine as the [[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 1971|#1 pop single of 1971]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/charts/yearend_chart_display.jsp?f=The+Billboard+Hot+100&g=Year-end+Singles&year=1971 |title=Year End Charts - Year-end Singles - The Billboard Hot 100 |publisher=Billboard.com |access-date=2009-08-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071103052401/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/charts/yearend_chart_display.jsp?f=The+Billboard+Hot+100&g=Year-end+Singles&year=1971 |archive-date=2007-11-03 |url-status=dead}}</ref> The song was also nominated for a [[Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals|Grammy Award for Best Pop Vocal Performance by a Duo Or Group]] during the [[14th Grammy Awards]].

The single went on to sell 5 million copies worldwide.<ref name=goldendiscs>{{cite book|title=The Book of Golden Discs|url=https://archive.org/details/bookofgoldendisc00murr|url-access=registration|quote=rudolph.|edition=2, illustrated|first=Joseph|last=Murrells|publisher=[[Barrie & Jenkins]]|isbn=0-214-20480-4|year=1978}}</ref>

The single had been out less than two months, when on April 9, 1971, "Joy to the World" was certified gold by the Recording Industry Association of America, for shipments of over one million units across the United States. The record was also given a Gold Leaf award by RPM magazine for sales of over a million units. The record won the award for the Best Selling Hit Single Record by the National Association of Recording Merchandisers in March 1972.
It was also ranked by Billboard magazine as the #1 pop single of 1971. The song was also nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Pop Vocal Performance by a Duo Or Group during the 14th Grammy Awards.

The single went on to sell 5 million copies worldwide.

sections.heading: Cover versions
sections.wikitext: Axton subsequently recorded his own version of the song for his album ''Joy to the World'' (1971). [[Little Richard]] recorded a cover of the song for his 1971 album, ''[[The King of Rock and Roll]]'', with a lengthy spoken intro and outro in the style of [[Black sermonic tradition]] preaching. The song has also been covered by [[Conway Twitty]], [[Lynn Anderson]], and others.
sections.text: Axton subsequently recorded his own version of the song for his album Joy to the World (1971). Little Richard recorded a cover of the song for his 1971 album, The King of Rock and Roll, with a lengthy spoken intro and outro in the style of Black sermonic tradition preaching. The song has also been covered by Conway Twitty, Lynn Anderson, and others.

sections.heading: Certifications
In popular culture
sections.wikitext:
{{more citations needed section|date=July 2024}}
*The song was used a variation of the opening theme in ''[[Joy Junction]]''.
*The song's refrain was used by [[Mariah Carey]] in her 1994 recording of the Christmas hymn "[[Joy to the World]]" on her album ''[[Merry Christmas (Mariah Carey album)|Merry Christmas]]''.
*In 1998, the song was referenced in ''[[Muppets Tonight]]'' during the episode "[[Andie MacDowell]]".
* In 2004, former ''[[Lizzie McGuire]]'' stars [[Hilary Duff]] and [[Davida Williams]] covered the song in their movie ''[[Raise Your Voice]]''. 
* Singer-songwriter [[Daniel Johnston]] liked the song, which inspired his own character Jeremiah the bullfrog, whom he often drew in his artwork and advertisements. The frog is also featured on the cover of his album ''[[Hi, How Are You]]'' (1983) and has become an official music mascot for Johnston.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lambiek.net/artists/j/johnston_daniel.htm|title=Daniel Johnston|website=Lambiek.net|access-date=26 December 2021}}</ref>
* The song was performed by the cast of ''[[Zoom (1972 TV series)|ZOOM]]'' during season 3.
* The chorus served as the finale to the Modern Times scene in Disneyland's [[America Sings]].
* It is sung by the son of one of the main characters at the start of the film ''[[The Big Chill (film)|The Big Chill]]'' (1983) and is featured on the soundtrack.
* The song was included in the film ''[[Forrest Gump]]'' and its [[Forrest Gump: The Soundtrack|soundtrack]].
* In ''[[The X-Files]]'' TV series ("[[Detour (The X-Files)|Detour]]" - S05E04), Scully sings the song to a wounded Mulder in the forest at night.
* The song's opening lyric "Jeremiah was a bullfrog" was used by [[Petey Pablo]] in his 2001 track "I Told Y'all" from his album ''[[Diary of a Sinner: 1st Entry]]''.
* It was the opening theme song for the 2002 [[Fuji TV]] series ''[[Lunch no Joō]]'', starring [[Yūko Takeuchi]] and [[Satoshi Tsumabuki]].
* In English translations of ''[[Animal Crossing]]'', there is a blue frog named Jeremiah (known as Quattro in its original Japanese), his English name coming from the first lyric.
* It is played during the end credits of the [[Adult animation|R-rated animated film]] ''[[Sausage Party]]'' (2016).
* It appears in 2017 and 2018 TV commercials for [[Big Lots]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ispot.tv/ad/wsUC/big-lots-joy-recliners-song-by-three-dog-night|title=Big Lots TV Commercial, 'Joy: Recliners' Song by Three Dog Night|website=Ispot.tv|access-date=December 24, 2017}}</ref>
* The song appears frequently in the movie ''[[28 Days (film)|28 Days]]'', including when Gwen Cummings ([[Sandra Bullock]]) finishes her stint in court-mandated rehab.
* It is played during the end credits of ''[[Drowning Mona]]''.
* There is a short fantasy story by John A. Pitts titled [https://dailysciencefiction.com/fantasy/modern-fantasy/john-a-pitts/jeremiah-was-a-bullfrog ''Jeremiah was a Bullfrog''], which reimagines the song.
* In the historical drama TV series ''[[Outlander (TV series)|Outlander]]'' (season 5, episode 2), Roger MacKenzie sings the song to his baby son Jeremiah.<ref>[https://www.cheatsheet.com/entertainment/outlander-season-5-richard-rankin-has-new-songs-for-roger-to-sing.html/ Outlander Season 5: Richard Rankin Has New Songs for Roger to Sing], Showbiz CheatSheet, February 19, 2020.</ref>
* It appears in the [[J.C. Penney]] 2020 seasonal holiday TV advertising campaign.
* The refrain to the song is sung briefly by elves in the 2004 movie [[Ella Enchanted (film)|Ella Enchanted]].
* In April 2006, the cast of the Nickelodeon shows ''[[Dora the Explorer (TV series)|Dora the Explorer]]'' and ''[[Go, Diego, Go!]]'' covered the song on the album ''Diego, Dora & Friends' Animals Jamboree''.
* In 2007, the song was featured at the end of the [[Sony Pictures Animation]] short, ''[[The ChubbChubbs!|The ChubbChubbs Save Xmas]]''.
* In September 2010, Nickelodeon covered the song again, this time with the [[Wonder Pets!|Wonder Pets]] for the ''2010 Mega Music Fest''.
* In the comic strip ''[[Zits (comics)|Zits]]'', the main character Jeremy Duncan once questioned his parent's reasons for giving him his name, when in a flashback, while pregnant with him; they attended a Three Dog Night concert and the band started playing the opening lyrics of the song, much to their own secret embarrassment.<ref>{{Cite web |title= Today's Zits, about naming kids|url=https://arnoldzwicky.org/2014/08/10/named-after/|access-date=2014-08-10 |website=arnoldzwicky.org|date=10 August 2014 |language=en}}</ref>
* The song and band are referenced by the American folk-rock group [[Fruit Bats (band)|Fruit Bats]] in their song "Singing Joy to the World," off their album ''[[The Ruminant Band]]''.
* The song appeared in the Cosmic Mix Vol. 1 of the [[Guardians of the Galaxy (TV series)|''Guardians of Galaxy'']] series. It was featured at the end of the episode "Bad Moon Rising".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Every song from S1E10 - Guardians of the Galaxy, "Bad Moon Rising" |url=https://www.what-song.com/Tvshow/100269/Guardians-of-the-Galaxy/e/109685 |access-date=2022-08-01 |website=WhatSong |language=en}}</ref>
*It is also played at the end of every [[Denver Broncos]] home victory. Notable playings of this song after Broncos victories included then-[[Chicago Bears]] head coach [[Abe Gibron]] singing along with the song in 1973 and at the end of [[Super Bowl XXXII]] at [[Qualcomm Stadium]] in [[San Diego]]. It was also played at the end of [[Super Bowl XXXIII]] at Pro Player Stadium (now [[Hard Rock Stadium]]) in [[Miami Gardens, Florida]] and [[Super Bowl 50]] in [[Santa Clara, California]].
* In ''[[Sex and the City]]'' (S02E10),  Carrie and her friend Jeremiah sing the song while drunk.
* In ''[[Friends]]'' (S09E13), Chandler sings the song at the karaoke.
* In the show ''[[Malcolm in the Middle]]'' (S04E15), the song is briefly heard on Hal's radio. 
*In the show ''[[The Last Man on Earth (TV series)|The Last Man on Earth]]'', the song is used with a singing fish animatronic as a security alarm.
* In the series ''[[The Summer I Turned Pretty (TV series)|The Summer I Turned Pretty]]'' (S03E07), Jeremiah and his friends sing the song at a bar.

* The song appeared in the Cosmic Mix Vol. 1 of the Guardians of Galaxy series. It was featured at the end of the episode "Bad Moon Rising".
*It is also played at the end of every Denver Broncos home victory. Notable playings of this song after Broncos victories included then-Chicago Bears head coach Abe Gibron singing along with the song in 1973 and at the end of Super Bowl XXXII at Qualcomm Stadium in San Diego. It was also played at the end of Super Bowl XXXIII at Pro Player Stadium (now Hard Rock Stadium) in Miami Gardens, Florida and Super Bowl 50 in Santa Clara, California.
* In Sex and the City (S02E10),  Carrie and her friend Jeremiah sing the song while drunk.
* In Friends (S09E13), Chandler sings the song at the karaoke.
* In the show Malcolm in the Middle (S04E15), the song is briefly heard on Hal's radio. 
*In the show The Last Man on Earth, the song is used with a singing fish animatronic as a security alarm.
* In the series The Summer I Turned Pretty (S03E07), Jeremiah and his friends sing the song at a bar.
